mateh-yehonatan.1#_: (siman 119 in Shulchan Aruch seif 1) One suspected of eating, etc. As explained in Shach s.k. 1 — but it is difficult, for in the new simanim in siman 1 the Mechaber ruled like Rambam at length; one must say there the matter does not depend on presumption of kosher status, for certainly the Mechaber holds one does not remove a person from presumption of kosher status; there the reason is we say he is not expert in a matter he thinks he is expert in all his laws and is not — therefore we do not remove him from presumption of kosher status; investigate.
mateh-yehonatan.2#_: (there seif 7) And regarding others' property, etc. They challenge from what we learned in chapter 4 of Demai: one who buys produce from one not trusted regarding tithes and forgot to tithe and asked on Shabbat — may eat on his word; after Shabbat dark he may not eat until he tithes, etc. — if so we learn even regarding others he is not believed at all. One must say there it deals when he said generically and did not say they are tithed; he said he saw he tithed the produce — he saw they are tithed for that produce; if so we are concerned he speaks in the language of Demai thinking they are tithed but in truth they are not — unlike if the suspected one said he saw they were tithed, one may say in truth even though he is suspected, regarding others we do not suspect him to lie intentionally. The Mechaber wrote he is believed regarding others — one may say when he said he saw the act, and this is believed by all; see Lechem Mishneh chapter 1 of Forbidden Foods chapter 3 law 21 see there.
mateh-yehonatan.3#_: (there in the gloss seif 7) One who is suspected, etc.; however regarding that matter he is not believed. As explained in Shach s.k. 9 who wrote the Rav's words need explanation, etc. see there; and I say to explain: certainly if one is suspected of eating one prohibition he is not suspected for every kind of prohibition only for that matter alone — if suspected of eating the "pants" of Rhine children where for them it is a karet prohibition we do not say he is suspected for all milk in the world, only we say he is believed for all milk except that matter itself, namely stomach-milk, regarding which he is not believed at all; investigate.
mateh-yehonatan.4#_: (there seif 19 in the gloss) And all this does not apply to one suspected of prohibition, etc. See Shach s.k. 37 end of the seif; still difficult, for in siman 86 the Rav wrote even a gentile selling eggs is believed when he says this is from such-and-such bird and pure though it is d'oraisa; one must say there in Avodah Zarah 63b the baraita permits buying eggs from gentiles everywhere without concern for nevelah or tereifah; Ran asks since most birds are pure why challenge; answer: minority of nevelah and tereifah combine with minority of impure bird for half-and-half — Ran; Tosafot; and it is known wherever there is fruit the minority is forbidden only d'rabbanan; therefore he is believed saying this bird and pure — requires study. [His words require study, for Ran wrote half-and-half or majority — if so it is d'oraisa doubt; requires study.]
